neurips-2021-modular-gaussian-processes-.tldr: Modular Gaussian processes transfer learned predictions and uncertainty without revisiting training data.
paragraphs: Transfer learning with Gaussian processes can become costly if combining models requires centralizing their original datasets. This paper instead treats fitted Gaussian processes as reusable modules, each represented by its hyperparameters, pseudo-inputs, and posterior densities.

The framework builds ensemble Gaussian-process models from a dictionary of such modules without returning to the observations. Its variational construction uses Kullback–Leibler divergence between stochastic processes to obtain an efficient lower bound across sparse variational models that may differ in complexity and likelihood distribution.

The method also supports multiple outputs and can learn correlations afterward between modules trained independently. Large-scale and multitask experiments illustrate its usefulness, including comparisons with exact-inference methods. The abstract gives no numerical results, but the operational contribution is explicit: reuse fitted model summaries and uncertainty information while avoiding the data centralization and repeated fitting that would otherwise accompany model combination.

neurips-2021-online-matching-in-sparse-r.tldr: A differential-equation analysis gives finite-size guarantees for greedy online matching in configuration-model graphs.
paragraphs: Online matching makes allocation decisions as opportunities arrive. This paper studies sparse random graphs whose vertices have fixed degree distributions, using the configuration model rather than assuming independent, identically distributed connections. That setting captures a different structure from many standard random-graph analyses.

The authors approximate relevant discrete stochastic processes with continuous processes described by an explicit system of partial differential equations. This provides estimates of GREEDY’s competitive ratio and precise approximation-error bounds that hold with arbitrarily high probability as problem size increases.

The technique permits formal comparisons between degree-distribution models. It also shows that GREEDY can have better performance guarantees than RANKING, despite the latter’s usual advantage in other settings. The result is therefore distribution-sensitive: it does not say GREEDY universally dominates RANKING, but demonstrates why online-matching guarantees can change when the graph-generation assumptions change.

neurips-2021-open-set-label-noise-can-im.tldr: Open-set examples with changing noisy labels can regularize classifiers trained on noisy datasets.
paragraphs: Examples outside the intended label set are usually treated as harmful label noise. This paper reports that such open-set noise can sometimes improve robustness to noise already present in a training dataset. It turns that observation into a regularizer called Open-set samples with Dynamic Noisy Labels, or ODNL.

The method introduces outside samples with changing noisy labels, aiming to consume excess network capacity without disrupting the learning of clean patterns. An analysis through stochastic-gradient noise characterizes the added noise and suggests it may favor stable, flatter solutions and more conservative out-of-distribution predictions.

Experiments across benchmark datasets and noise types improve several existing robust-learning algorithms and out-of-distribution detection. The proposed convergence explanation is presented as a possible mechanism, not proof that every run reaches a flat minimum. The abstract does not justify adding arbitrary mislabeled data indiscriminately; the reported benefits belong to this particular regularization procedure.

neurips-2021-optimal-best-arm-identifica.tldr: Tail-risk best-arm identification attains asymptotically optimal sample counts under the studied distributional model.
paragraphs: Choosing an option by its mean can overlook rare but costly outcomes. This paper studies identifying the best arm among finitely many alternatives using value-at-risk, conditional value-at-risk, or a weighted combination of conditional value-at-risk and the mean.

The authors give a delta-correct algorithm for general arms, including heavy-tailed distributions. Its expected number of samples matches the lower bound asymptotically as delta approaches zero. Implementing the method involves a nonconvex optimization problem over probability measures, so the statistical result is accompanied by substantial analytical work.

The paper also develops nonasymptotic, anytime-valid concentration inequalities for tail-risk measures using empirical likelihood. These support reasoning about uncertainty throughout sequential sampling. The optimality statement concerns the asymptotic confidence regime and the paper’s model, rather than a claim of finite-sample optimality or easy computation for every conceivable heavy-tailed decision problem.

neurips-2021-optimal-uniform-ope-and-mod.tldr: Local uniform policy-evaluation bounds unify several model-based offline reinforcement-learning guarantees.
paragraphs: Offline policy evaluation estimates policy values from a fixed dataset. Uniform evaluation controls error across a policy class and can support learning, but covering every policy may require substantially more data than covering policies close to empirically optimal.

For episodic models with stationary transitions, the paper proves a global model-based lower bound of Omega(H²S/(d_m epsilon²)) and a local upper bound of roughly O(H²/(d_m epsilon²)), up to logarithmic factors. Here d_m is the minimum marginal state-action probability. A new singleton-absorbing-MDP construction enables the sharper local analysis.

The framework extends to task-agnostic and reward-free offline learning, with respective complexities roughly O(H² log(K)/(d_m epsilon²)) and O(H²S/(d_m epsilon²)). K is the number of tasks. These are statistical guarantees under the specified coverage and transition assumptions; the abstract does not report empirical performance or suggest that arbitrary offline datasets provide adequate coverage.

neurips-2021-privately-publishable-per-i.tldr: Per-instance privacy losses from objective perturbation can themselves be released privately.
paragraphs: Differential privacy gives a worst-case guarantee that can be much larger than the actual loss for one individual in a particular dataset. Per-instance differential privacy offers a more personalized assessment, but that assessment may itself depend on sensitive data and therefore cannot automatically be published safely.

This paper analyzes per-instance privacy loss for an empirical-risk minimizer released using objective perturbation. It then develops methods for privately publishing those individualized loss values, addressing the privacy of the assessment as well as the privacy of the original model.

The proposed methods aim for accurate publication at little or no additional privacy cost. The abstract does not state exact bounds, assumptions, or empirical results, so the claim should remain specific to the analyzed objective-perturbation setting. The contribution is a way to make finer-grained privacy accounting available without overlooking the information that the accounting report can itself reveal.

neurips-2021-remips-physically-consisten.tldr: REMIPS reconstructs interacting people jointly while modeling contact and avoiding implausible mesh collisions.
paragraphs: Reconstructing several people from one image is difficult when their bodies are close or touching. Independent reconstructions miss interaction context, while joint methods can still produce implausible overlaps. REMIPS addresses a variable number of people under weak supervision.

Its transformer combines unordered person tokens with position-encoded image-patch tokens. A unified collision model uses decimated mesh approximations to handle both self-penetration and inter-person penetration. Self-supervised losses, including self-contact and interaction-contact terms, incorporate physical plausibility directly into learning.

The authors report state-of-the-art quantitative benchmark results even in cases without three-dimensional supervision. Qualitative examples from challenging natural images show coherent poses, shapes, and interactions. The abstract does not give scores or guarantee physical consistency in every reconstruction. Its central contribution is a joint image-and-person representation coupled with explicit collision and contact modeling for interacting humans.

neurips-2021-shapley-residuals-quantifyi.tldr: Shapley residuals quantify prediction structure that additive feature attributions leave unexplained.
paragraphs: Shapley-based explanations assign additive credit to features even when a model behaves nonlinearly. That simplification can lose information about the cooperative game used to define feature importance. This paper asks how to measure what the resulting attributions fail to capture.

The authors interpret Shapley values as an orthogonal projection between vector spaces. They compute a residual representing the component discarded by that projection, provide an algorithm for obtaining it, and characterize modeling settings according to the residual’s value.

Demonstrations show that these residuals contain information about model predictions absent from the Shapley values themselves. The abstract gives no benchmark metrics or threshold for acceptable explanation quality. The contribution is a diagnostic of the limits of an additive explanation, helping practitioners avoid treating a set of feature scores as a complete description of the model’s behavior.

neurips-2021-the-clear-benchmark-continu.tldr: CLEAR evaluates continual image learning using naturally evolving imagery and future-facing test protocols.
paragraphs: Continual-learning benchmarks often create artificial changes between tasks that may not resemble real temporal change. CLEAR instead uses imagery spanning 2004–2014 from YFCC100M, capturing a decade of evolving visual concepts. It includes labeled examples and abundant unlabeled images for each period.

The curation pipeline uses pretrained vision-language models such as CLIP for interactive dataset construction, followed by crowdsourced validation. Experiments show that a simple unsupervised pretraining step can improve continual-learning algorithms that otherwise use only supervised data.

The authors also find that conventional training and testing on identically distributed data inflate performance estimates. They propose streaming protocols that test on the near future and allow today’s test data to become later training data. The contribution combines a temporally grounded dataset with an evaluation design intended to better measure adaptation, rather than treating artificially separated static tasks as sufficient evidence of lifelong learning.

neurips-2021-unsupervised-object-level-r.tldr: ORL discovers object correspondences to improve self-supervised learning from complex scene images.
paragraphs: Contrastive image pretraining often assumes two augmented views depict the same object. That assumption fits curated object-centered images but can fail in scenes containing many objects. Object-level Representation Learning, or ORL, seeks to learn useful features without requiring that object-centric dataset structure.

The framework uses image-level self-supervised pretraining as a prior for discovering semantic correspondences at the object level. Those correspondences then support learning object representations directly from scene images, extending the training signal beyond whole-image similarity.

Experiments on COCO show substantial improvements in self-supervised learning from scenes, even surpassing supervised ImageNet pretraining on several downstream tasks. Adding more unlabeled scene images further improves downstream performance. The abstract does not list exact tasks or scores, so the supported result is the framework’s demonstrated transfer benefit, rather than a guarantee that every scene collection automatically yields better representations.

neurips-2022-agreement-on-the-line-predi.tldr: Agreement between neural classifiers can estimate accuracy on unlabeled shifted data.
paragraphs: In some benchmarks, in-distribution accuracy predicts out-of-distribution accuracy through a strong linear relationship. But that alone does not reveal the actual shifted accuracy without labeled validation data. This paper studies a related observable quantity: how often pairs of neural classifiers agree.

The authors find that when accuracy follows this relationship, agreement on shifted data also correlates linearly with in-distribution agreement. The slope and intercept closely match the corresponding accuracy relationship. Since agreement needs only predictions, it can be measured on unlabeled target data.

The resulting accuracy-estimation algorithm outperforms previous methods both where the relationship holds and in some cases where accuracy does not lie on the expected line. The authors observe the agreement phenomenon specifically for neural classifiers. These are empirical regularities and comparisons, not an unconditional guarantee that agreement reliably measures accuracy under every distribution shift.

neurips-2022-avlen-audio-visual-language.tldr: AVLEN learns when an audio-visual navigation agent should ask for natural-language help.
paragraphs: An embodied agent locating a sound source may encounter unfamiliar sounds, distractors, or ambiguous actions. AVLEN combines audio-visual navigation with the ability to request free-form language assistance from a human oracle, making help-seeking part of the navigation policy.

A hierarchical reinforcement-learning system uses a high-level policy to choose between following audio cues and querying the oracle. Lower-level policies choose movement actions from audio, vision, and language inputs. Training rewards navigation success while discouraging unnecessary queries.

Experiments use SoundSpaces for semantic audio-visual navigation. Asking for help improves performance, especially with sounds not heard during training or with distracting sounds present. The abstract does not provide success rates or the number of queries required. Its contribution is a learned balance between autonomous multimodal navigation and targeted assistance, evaluated within the stated simulated navigation framework.

neurips-2022-bimlp-compact-binary-archit.tldr: BiMLP strengthens binary vision MLPs with multibranch blocks and improved information flow.
paragraphs: Binarizing a vision multilayer perceptron can sharply limit its representational capacity. This paper analyzes why existing binarization methods perform poorly, emphasizing that fully connected layers resemble 1-by-1 convolutions and become restrictive for spatial and channel mixing when reduced to binary operations.

BiMLP introduces binary blocks with multiple branches that combine outputs from the same stage. A universal shortcut carries information from the preceding stage, and carefully designed downsampling layers reduce computation while preserving classification performance.

On ImageNet-1k, the proposed models achieve state-of-the-art accuracy compared with prior binary convolutional networks. The abstract does not give accuracy values, model sizes, or hardware timings. The contribution is therefore an architectural response to the capacity limitations of binary MLPs, with image-classification evidence, rather than a claim that binarization preserves the full performance of arbitrary real-valued models.

neurips-2022-class-dependent-label-noise.tldr: Cycle consistency improves estimation of class-dependent label-noise transitions.
paragraphs: Learning with class-dependent label noise often requires estimating a transition matrix from clean classes to noisy labels. Existing minimum-volume approaches rely heavily on estimated noisy-class probabilities, which can be inaccurate when deep networks overfit corrupted labels.

This paper proposes forward-backward cycle-consistency regularization for transition-matrix estimation. The regularizer indirectly encourages minimum volume without directly using the estimated noisy-class posterior in that step, reducing sensitivity to that source of error and encouraging convergence toward the desired transition matrix.

Experiments consistently reduce transition-matrix estimation error and improve classification performance. The abstract describes the relationship to sufficiently scattered assumptions in prior consistent estimation, but does not provide the full assumptions of its own guarantees or quantitative gains. The work addresses a specific bottleneck in noise-model estimation rather than claiming that arbitrary label corruption can always be corrected.

neurips-2022-cross-linked-unified-embedd.tldr: CLUE learns cross-modal representations even when some measurements are missing.
paragraphs: Multimodal data combine shared information with details specific to each measurement type, but many samples lack one or more modalities. CLUE, or Cross-Linked Unified Embedding, is a semisupervised neural model designed to learn useful representations from these incomplete observations.

The method extends multimodal variational autoencoders with cross-encoders that construct latent representations when modalities are missing. The paper focuses on single-cell measurements, where DNA, RNA, and protein provide related but distinct views of cellular function.

Benchmarks show superior performance in all assessed categories of the NeurIPS 2021 Multimodal Single-cell Data Integration Competition. The abstract does not provide category-level scores or quantify missing-data patterns. Although the cross-linked strategy is proposed as applicable to other multimodal tasks, the reported evidence is from single-cell genomics; broader applicability remains a plausible extension rather than an experimentally established result in every domain.

neurips-2022-debiased-causal-tree-hetero.tldr: Historical controls help regularize causal trees against unmeasured confounding under a transportability assumption.
paragraphs: Unobserved confounders can make treatment-effect estimates from observational data misleading. This paper supplements current observations with historical controls and proves partial identifiability of conditional average treatment effects on the treated under an interpretable transportability condition.

The authors introduce confounding entropy to quantify discrepancies between treated and control outcome distributions associated with hidden confounding. A debiased causal tree chooses splits by minimizing empirical risk regularized by this quantity, using current data for prediction risk and historical controls for the confounding term.

They also discuss robustness to population imbalance when confounders are observed and extend the method through gradient boosting. Simulations and a credit-card-balance study demonstrate computational feasibility and statistical effectiveness. The result depends on the transportability condition and available historical controls; it does not establish unrestricted causal identification from observational data despite arbitrary hidden confounding.

neurips-2022-earthformer-exploring-space.tldr: Earthformer uses cuboid attention to forecast spatiotemporal Earth-system data.
paragraphs: Earth-system forecasting traditionally relies on computationally demanding physical simulation. Growing observational datasets motivate learned alternatives, but applying Transformers effectively to space-time data requires attention mechanisms suited to that structure. Earthformer introduces such an architecture for forecasting.

Its Cuboid Attention block partitions the data into space-time cuboids and applies self-attention within them in parallel. A collection of global vectors connects the cuboids, allowing information exchange beyond each local block. MovingMNIST and a newly proposed chaotic N-body MNIST dataset support architectural investigation.

On two real-world benchmarks, precipitation nowcasting and El Niño/Southern Oscillation forecasting, Earthformer achieves state-of-the-art results. The abstract gives no forecast horizons, scores, or comparison with operational physical systems. The contribution is an efficient, flexible space-time attention design with evidence on those benchmarks, rather than a claim to replace all numerical weather and climate modeling.

neurips-2022-flashattention-fast-and-mem.tldr: FlashAttention accelerates exact attention by reducing movement between GPU memory levels.
paragraphs: Attention on long sequences can be slow because of memory traffic as well as arithmetic. FlashAttention organizes exact attention with tiling to reduce reads and writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM. Its analysis proves fewer high-bandwidth-memory accesses and optimality over a range of SRAM sizes.

The supplied abstract reports a 3x speedup on GPT-2 at sequence length 1K and 2.4x on Long Range Arena at lengths 1K–4K. It also describes an approximate extension. Some result sentences are fragmented, so the precise training configurations require the linked paper.

Reported quality outcomes include 0.7 better GPT-2 perplexity and 6.4 points on long-document classification. Long-sequence demonstrations achieve 61.4% on Path-X at length 16K and 63.1% on Path-256 at length 64K. The central algorithm computes exact attention; these broader quality gains concern the enabled experimental systems rather than changing the mathematical attention operation itself.

neurips-2022-forecasting-future-world-ev.tldr: Autocast benchmarks future-event forecasting while controlling access to time-stamped news.
paragraphs: Forecasting future events requires judging uncertain developments, often with substantial expert input. This paper introduces Autocast to test whether language models can help automate that task, using thousands of questions drawn from forecasting tournaments and an accompanying news corpus.

The news is organized by date so experiments can reproduce the information available when a historical forecast was made, avoiding leakage from later events. The authors also introduce IntervalQA, a numerical-question dataset with calibration metrics, motivated by quantities that vary across orders of magnitude.

Tested language models perform far below a human-expert baseline. Larger models and access to relevant news improve results, but do not close the reported gap. The abstract does not provide forecast scores. The contribution is a challenging evaluation resource and an initial assessment of capabilities, rather than evidence that language models already match experts on consequential future-event predictions.

neurips-2022-generalised-mutual-informat.tldr: GEMINI replaces mutual information’s core divergence to build more flexible clustering objectives.
paragraphs: Mutual information is widely used to train deep clustering models, often with substantial regularization. This paper examines the objective itself and argues that maximizing it can produce unsatisfactory clusters, identifying its Kullback–Leibler-divergence structure as a source of the behavior.

The authors introduce generalized mutual information, or GEMINI, by replacing that core distance. The resulting family supplies unsupervised objectives, some of which incorporate data geometry through distances or kernels. Some variants do not require the regularizers used with ordinary mutual information.

The paper also highlights automatic selection of a relevant number of clusters, an important issue when the cluster count is unknown beforehand. The abstract gives no dataset results or universal cluster-recovery guarantee. Its contribution is a family of alternative objectives and an analysis of their properties, inviting evaluation of clustering quality through more than the choice of regularization alone.

neurips-2022-generating-long-videos-of-d.tldr: A two-stage video generator learns long-term dynamics while retaining high-resolution output detail.
paragraphs: Long generated videos must introduce new content while preserving plausible motion and persistent objects. Existing approaches can become nearly static when one latent code fixes content, or drift unrealistically between scenes when long-term consistency is weak. This paper redesigns the temporal representation to address those competing failures.

The model emphasizes the time axis and learns consistency from longer training videos. A two-phase strategy separates learning from long low-resolution videos and from short high-resolution videos, allowing temporal extent and visual detail to be handled at different stages.

The authors also introduce two benchmark datasets focused explicitly on long-term temporal dynamics. The abstract describes realistic object motion, viewpoint changes, and emerging content, but provides no quantitative comparisons or duration limits. The contribution combines a temporal generation design, training strategy, and evaluation resources aimed at assessing behavior over time rather than judging isolated frames alone.

neurips-2022-global-convergence-of-direc.tldr: Direct policy search can reach a global optimum in the studied nonsmooth H-infinity control problem.
paragraphs: H-infinity robust control seeks a policy minimizing the closed-loop H-infinity norm. Directly searching over stabilizing state-feedback policies produces a constrained, nonconvex, nonsmooth problem, so standard intuition offers little assurance of finding the best controller.

This paper proves that every Clarke stationary point of the specified problem is a global minimum. It also establishes coerciveness of the objective and compactness of its sublevel sets, properties that help control the behavior of optimization iterates despite the nonconvex feasible region.

Using these facts, the authors show that Goldstein’s subgradient method and implementable variants can remain within the stabilizing-policy set and eventually reach a global optimum. The result concerns this H-infinity state-feedback synthesis formulation; it does not assert global convergence for arbitrary reinforcement-learning policy search. The contribution is a theoretical bridge between nonsmooth optimization and a fundamental robust-control design problem.

neurips-2022-iso-dream-isolating-and-lev.tldr: Iso-Dream separates action-controlled dynamics from independent motion to improve visual planning.
paragraphs: Visual environments contain both changes caused by an agent’s actions and changes that happen independently, such as other vehicles moving. A world model that entangles them can make planning difficult. Iso-Dream explicitly separates controllable and noncontrollable dynamics in a learned latent representation.

The model uses a three-branch architecture and an inverse-dynamics task to factor representations according to their response to actions. During behavior learning, it rolls noncontrollable states forward and associates those predictions with the current controllable state when estimating value.

Experiments across visual-control and prediction domains show effective separation of the mixed dynamics and substantial improvements over existing methods. The abstract does not provide benchmark scores or demonstrate deployment in autonomous driving; that example motivates the method’s potential. The supported result is improved planning and prediction within the evaluated domains through explicit treatment of motion that the agent does not control.

neurips-2022-iterative-scene-graph-gener.tldr: Iterative scene-graph refinement jointly reasons about objects and their relationships.
paragraphs: Scene-graph generation identifies objects and the relationships between them in images or video. Fixed factorization assumptions can make prediction manageable, but may miss cases where recognizing an object depends on understanding its interaction with something else, especially when the object is small or unclear.

This paper uses message passing in a Markov random field and dynamic conditioning on the image. An end-to-end transformer architecture repeatedly refines the graph, with each update conditioned on the previous graph. That feedback supports joint reasoning over entities and relations.

Experiments on Visual Genome and Action Genome show improved scene-graph generation, and the framework can also improve existing approaches. The abstract does not report quantitative gains or iteration costs. The contribution is an iterative alternative to one fixed prediction factorization, allowing provisional relationships and object identities to inform each other during refinement.

neurips-2022-lower-bounds-on-randomly-pr.tldr: Randomized invertible preconditioning cannot remove certain sample barriers for Lasso.
paragraphs: Sparse regression with ill-conditioned Gaussian covariates is suspected to have a gap between statistical possibility and computationally accessible methods. Prior lower bounds for preconditioned Lasso applied only to deterministic preconditioners. This paper extends the limitation to randomized invertible preconditioning.

For a suitable covariance matrix, the authors construct one signal distribution on which any invertibly preconditioned Lasso fails with high probability unless it receives a linear number of samples. This strengthens evidence about the limits of that broad algorithmic family, rather than ruling out every possible regression algorithm.

The proof develops a robustness result for sparse compressed-sensing measurements under adversarial erasures. With standard sparse Bernoulli measurements, erasing b measurements leaves all but O(b) signal coordinates identifiable. The connection is notable because a positive robustness property in sparse recovery helps establish a negative sample-complexity result for preconditioned Lasso.
